page_title: OLIV: Thai + English voice typing for Mac

summary.name: OLIV
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac dictation app for mixing Thai and English speech that types the English words in English, running on-device.
keywords: dictation for slack and vs code
use_cases: Dictating Thai messages that contain English terms or jargon
Typing English technical words by voice while speaking Thai
Dictating into Slack, VS Code, Notes or other Mac apps
Offline voice typing without sending audio to the cloud
Adding custom vocabulary and replacements for names and acronyms
summary.what_it_does: OLIV is a Mac dictation app: you hold a key (Right ⌥ by default), speak, and release, and the transcribed text is pasted at the cursor in any app. It transcribes with Typhoon Whisper Turbo, a Whisper model tuned for Thai, then applies a dictionary and sound-alike matching for known words, formats Thai numbers, and uses a small language model (Gemma E2B) to turn Thai-spelled English jargon back into English. It supports custom vocabulary, replacements, a choice of three speech engines, and an optional cloud engine (Groq or a self-hosted OLIV API server) that is off until enabled. The page reports benchmarks on 264 self-recorded clips, including 97% meaning-preservation versus 93% for Wispr Flow, but these were recorded by one speaker.
notable: Restores English words that speech models would otherwise spell in Thai letters
Runs on-device with offline dictation after a one-time ~5 GB model download
MIT-licensed, no subscription, no telemetry, benchmark code on GitHub
Verbatim mode for apps that should receive the raw transcript
caveats: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 or later
Benchmarks use a single speaker in a quiet room; other voices, accents and noisy settings are untested
First launch downloads about 5 GB of models; cloud engines are optional and send audio off-device
